title: Configure, Certify, and Operate Kubernetes GPU Clusters with NVIDIA DSX OS | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA presents DSX OS, the open-source (Apache 2.0) software layer of its DSX AI Factory Platform, comprising AICR for version-locked Kubernetes configuration recipes, NVCRE for workload-based cluster certification, and NVSentinel for continuous health monitoring and remediation. The core argument is that one-time cluster certification goes stale and goodput, not utilization, should measure GPU cluster efficiency.

insights.claim: A single underperforming GPU can slow an entire synchronous distributed training job to its slowest rank while passing basic health checks and showing normal utilization, so operators may only discover it hours later.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Hidden performance degradation erodes the effective return on GPU capex, making validation tooling valuable to GPU cloud operators.
insights.quote: One underperforming GPU can slow an entire distributed training job.

insights.claim: NVIDIA argues goodput, the volume of work successfully completed, is a better measure of cluster efficiency than utilization metrics, which can mask losses from failing nodes and healthy nodes left idle out of caution.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Shifts the KPI investors and operators should use when assessing GPU cloud efficiency claims.
insights.quote: Goodput, which is the volume of work successfully completed, provides a more useful measure of cluster efficiency.

insights.claim: A GPU cluster certified at handover drifts as nodes are replaced, drivers patched and capacity added, so readiness requires repeated validation throughout the cluster lifecycle.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Creates an ongoing operational-software need rather than a one-time acceptance test.

insights.claim: NVIDIA DSX OS is the open-source software layer of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, with three Apache 2.0 projects mapped to configure (AICR), certify (NVCRE) and operate (NVSentinel).
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is open-sourcing AI factory operations software to deepen ecosystem dependence on its Kubernetes stack.
insights.locator: The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform

insights.claim: NVIDIA is promoting DSX OS through a workshop at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America, a booth and a Slack community, targeting the cloud-native Kubernetes community.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Indicates NVIDIA's push to become the default GPU layer in cloud-native infrastructure.

insights.claim: AICR resolves a target environment (e.g. EKS, H100, Ubuntu, inference, Dynamo) against validated overlays into a recipe that pins component versions, declares a dependency graph and attaches per-component health assertions.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Version-locked reference stacks reduce deployment friction for NVIDIA GPUs on hyperscaler Kubernetes.

insights.claim: AICR renders recipes into artifacts for existing deployers including Helm, Argo CD, Flux and Helmfile, so operators keep their current tooling.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Complements rather than displaces existing GitOps tools, easing adoption.

insights.claim: AICR's diff command with --fail-on-drift turns configuration-drift detection into a CI gate that can trigger recertification after driver, operator or fabric changes, which do not trigger revalidation automatically.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Operational discipline features target enterprise and neocloud operators managing frequent upgrades.

insights.claim: NVCRE certifies clusters by running NCCL communication tests, DCGM level 4 diagnostics and NeMo Framework pretraining workloads with 8B- and 56B-parameter models, rather than relying on standard service health checks.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Workload-level acceptance testing may become a standard in GPU cluster procurement and handover.

insights.claim: NVCRE ships with no performance thresholds by default, so without configured thresholds such as bus bandwidth of at least 300 GB/s, a node performing below target can still pass.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Certification quality depends on operator configuration; default runs catch breakage, not degradation.
insights.quote: Thresholds help catch performance degradation rather than breakage.

insights.claim: When a large all-reduce such as a 64-node test yields poor bandwidth, NVCRE automatically bisects failing groups down to a minimum size and reports suspect nodes with reasons.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Automated fault isolation shortens downtime on large clusters, improving goodput.

insights.claim: NVSentinel monitors existing signals such as DCGM health checks, Xid errors, NIC states and cloud provider maintenance events without consuming GPU time, and installs in monitoring-only mode by default.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Low-friction rollout lowers barriers to adoption on live production clusters.

insights.claim: NVSentinel uses CEL-based fault quarantine rulesets to cordon or taint nodes, with a circuit breaker capping how many GPU nodes can be quarantined in a sliding window, and a health events analyzer flagging repeatedly failing nodes.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Guardrails against mass quarantine address a key risk of automated remediation at scale.

insights.claim: The NVSentinel lifecycle controller automatically gates new or remediated nodes until NVCRE tests pass, so a node failing validation cannot silently rejoin the pool.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Closing the repair-to-production loop reduces manual SRE handoffs and the wasted compute from bad nodes.

insights.claim: NVIDIA deliberately separates roles: NVCRE stops at attribution while NVSentinel owns quarantine and repair, allowing platform teams to replace NVSentinel with their own lifecycle tooling.
insights.speaker: Sowmyan Soman
insights.so_what: Modularity aims to let large operators adopt pieces of DSX OS without full lock-in.
